`propTypes` check the props they name and say nothing about the rest. A misspelled prop such as `onclick` is passed, ignored, and never noticed. A wrapper such as `exact()` from the `prop-types-exact` package adds a warning for every prop that is not declared.

The rule does nothing until you name your wrapper. List it under `propWrapperFunctions` in the `settings` of your ESLint config, with `exact: true`:

{/* skip */}
```js
import react from "eslint-plugin-react";

export default [
  {
    plugins: { react },
    rules: { "react/prefer-exact-props": "error" },
    settings: {
      propWrapperFunctions: [{ property: "exact", exact: true }],
    },
  },
];
```

## Examples

Reported, with the config above:

{/* bad {"config": "oxlint", "settings": {"propWrapperFunctions": [{"property": "exact", "exact": true}]}} */}
```jsx
function Button({ label }) {
  return <button>{label}</button>;
}

Button.propTypes = {
  label: PropTypes.string,
};
```

{/* bad {"config": "oxlint", "settings": {"propWrapperFunctions": [{"property": "exact", "exact": true}]}} */}
```jsx
class Button extends React.Component {
  static propTypes = {
    label: PropTypes.string,
  };
  render() {
    return <button>{this.props.label}</button>;
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good {"config": "oxlint", "settings": {"propWrapperFunctions": [{"property": "exact", "exact": true}]}} */}
```jsx
function Button({ label }) {
  return <button>{label}</button>;
}

Button.propTypes = exact({
  label: PropTypes.string,
});
```
